# Purpose and scope

This Process Characterization Plan (**PCP-007**) defines the Stage 1 (Process Design)
characterization of the A-Mab cation-exchange (CEX) polishing chromatography step
(Step 7), the bind-and-elute polishing operation that follows low-pH viral
inactivation. CEX is the **principal aggregate-reduction (polish) step** of the
purification train — the only step that actively reduces high-molecular-weight
aggregate — and provides a major further reduction of host-cell protein (HCP), and
modular clearance of residual DNA and leached Protein A. The plan specifies the
objectives, the attributes in scope, the process parameters and ranges to be
characterized, the experimental designs, the analytical methods, the sampling plan,
the statistical-analysis approach, and the acceptance and decision criteria by which
each parameter will be classified and a multivariate operating region established.

**Scope.** The commercial-scale cation-exchange polishing step, characterized on a
qualified scale-down chromatography column. The upstream low-pH viral-inactivation step
(Step 6), which defines the feed to this step, and the downstream anion-exchange step
(Step 8), which provides the subsequent polish, are addressed only where they define the
feed to, or clear the impurity load from, this step; their characterization is out of
scope. This plan governs execution only — the results are reported in the paired Process
Characterization Report (**PCR-007**).

**Basis.** The unit-operation model, quality-attribute framework and risk methodology
follow the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]; the Stage 1 approach and report structure
follow the FDA 2011 guidance [@fda2011] and the ICH Q8–Q11 [@fda2011]; the QbD
framework follows ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11] and the lifecycle
approach of the FDA 2011 guidance [@fda2011].

# Objectives

The characterization will:

1. establish the quantitative relationships between the cation-exchange process
   parameters and the eluate-pool aggregate, the eluate-pool HCP and the step yield;
2. identify the significant main effects, two-factor interactions and curvature,
   including the anticipated protein-load × wash-conductivity interaction that governs
   HCP clearance;
3. define the multivariate operating region over which the eluate-pool aggregate and HCP
   presented to the anion-exchange step are controlled;
4. establish proven acceptable ranges (PARs) and confirm normal operating ranges
   (NORs) for each parameter;
5. classify each parameter for its risk of impact to CQAs and to process performance
   (CPP / WC-CPP / KPP / GPP); and
6. provide the process understanding and ranges that justify the Stage 2 operating
   conditions and the drug-substance control strategy.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

Cation-exchange chromatography is the first polishing step of the A-Mab purification
train: the neutralized viral-inactivation pool is loaded onto a strong cation-exchange
resin at controlled conductivity, weakly bound impurities are removed in the wash, and
the product is recovered by an ascending-pH (or ascending-salt) elution, with the eluate
pool collected between defined start and stop criteria [@amab2009]. Unlike the upstream
operations it forms no new product-quality CQA; its role in the control strategy is to
**reduce the high-molecular-weight aggregate** carried into the pool — including the
aggregate that can arise during the upstream low-pH hold — and to provide a major further
reduction of HCP and modular clearance of residual DNA and leached Protein A. Platform
knowledge established that aggregate, being more highly charged and more strongly
retained, is separated from monomer in the elution so that the pool aggregate rises with
higher protein load and as the elution pool is extended further down the descending edge
(a higher stop-collect) and at higher elution pH; that HCP clearance is governed by the
load/wash conductivity — a higher conductivity strips more weakly bound HCP before
elution — and falls at high load, the two acting together through a load × conductivity
interaction; and that recovery declines modestly at high load. This knowledge frames the
attributes in scope and the prioritization of parameters for characterization.

## Quality attributes in scope

Cation exchange introduces no CQA. It is the principal reduction step for the
high-molecular-weight aggregate and a major clearance step for the impurity CQAs formed
upstream and specified at the drug substance (@tbl-cqa). Criticality is scored on the
A-Mab continuum using Tool #1 (Risk Score = Impact × Uncertainty); attributes rated High
(H) or Very High (VH) are treated as *Critical* [@amab2009; @ichq9].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(CEX_CQAS))
```

: CQAs controlled by the cation-exchange step (formed upstream; polished/cleared here), with acceptance criterion and criticality (Tool #1 = Impact × Uncertainty). {#tbl-cqa}

The eluate-pool aggregate and eluate-pool HCP are not themselves released specifications;
they are in-process attributes whose control at this step determines the size-variant and
impurity load presented to the anion-exchange step and therefore the margin to the
≤ `{python} f"{agg_acc_hi:g}"`% HMW aggregate and ≤ `{python} hcp_acc_hi` ng/mg HCP
drug-substance limits. Because aggregate can be elevated in the incoming pool, the study
is designed to demonstrate the aggregate-clearance capacity of the step against a
representative, deliberately challenging aggregate feed; pool aggregate is the primary
response of the study.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

Consistent with the A-Mab lifecycle of iterative risk assessments and the risk flow of
the FDA 2011 guidance, the study scope is set by the Pre-Characterization Process Risk Assessment
(**RA-001**). A risk-ranking-and-filtering (RRF) screen scores each parameter for its
potential main-effect and interaction impact and assigns the study type accordingly:
protein load, load/wash conductivity, elution pH and the elution stop-collect — which
carry a credible main-effect and interaction risk to the eluate-pool aggregate or HCP —
are studied in the multivariate DoE; the elution flow rate, expected to affect only
process performance over a wide range, is studied univariately [@amab2009]. The resulting
parameter set and study-type assignment are given in @tbl-param.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

Characterization will be performed on a scale-down cation-exchange column operated at the
commercial-process equivalents for resin, bed height, residence time, buffer system, load
ratio and elution strategy (**SOP-2010**, **SOP-2008**). Prior to characterization the
SDM will be qualified against at-scale reference data (**SOP-1001**) by comparing the
operational parameters and, critically, the input and output attributes — step yield,
eluate-pool aggregate and HCP, residual DNA and leached Protein A — to confirm the model
is representative and suitable to support operating-range and PAR claims [@fda2011]. The
centre-point replicates of each design provide an in-study estimate of model
reproducibility (pure error) used in the lack-of-fit assessment.

## Operation

The neutralized viral-inactivation pool is conditioned to the target load conductivity
and loaded onto the equilibrated cation-exchange column to the target load ratio; the
column is washed at the load/wash conductivity to remove weakly bound host-cell protein
and other impurities; and the product is recovered by elution, with the eluate pool
collected from a defined start until the descending-edge stop-collect criterion. Buffers,
resin lot and column packing are controlled to platform specifications (**SOP-2008**) and
are treated as identity/quality-controlled inputs rather than characterized variables
[@amab2009].

## Analytical methods

The step responses will be measured by the validated methods in @tbl-methods; method
performance characteristics are per the cited validation reports. Aggregate is determined
by SEC-HPLC, the primary assay for the aggregate-polish claim.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=[], amvs=CEX_AMV_REFS))
```

: Validated analytical methods for the characterization. {#tbl-methods}

## Sampling plan

Each DoE run will be sampled at the eluate pool for aggregate, HCP, residual DNA and
leached Protein A, and the load and pool product mass will be recorded for the step-yield
determination; in-process readings (pH, conductivity, UV) will confirm the chromatographic
profile and the pool collection window. Centre-point runs are replicated within each
design (three in screening, four in the response-surface design) to quantify
reproducibility and pure error.

## Statistical methods

Designs will be constructed and analyzed in coded factors, with each parameter's
characterization range mapped so that the set-point is 0 and the range edges are
±1 (**SOP-1002**). Screening data will be analyzed by ordinary-least-squares regression
of each response on the main effects and all two-factor interactions; factor effects are
reported as twice the coded coefficient. Response-surface data will be analyzed with the
full quadratic model (main effects, two-factor interactions and pure-quadratic terms).
Significance will be assessed at α = 0.05. Model adequacy will be judged by R², adjusted
R², predicted R² (from the PRESS statistic), the overall model F-test, and an ANOVA
lack-of-fit test against the centre-point pure error; a response with no significant
parameter effect beyond a single dominant factor will be reported as robust rather than
modelled predictively. The operating region will be defined as the multivariate region of
the well-controlled CPPs over which the eluate-pool aggregate and HCP are controlled, and
commercial-scale capability of the drug-substance CQAs governed by the step will be
estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation with each parameter varied within its NOR.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and study type

Five parameters are in scope (@tbl-param). The characterization range of each factor
("Range studied") defines the edges of the explored knowledge space and the basis of the
PAR; the NOR is the tighter routine-control range. Classification is an output of the
study and is reported in PCR-007. The DoE factor coding for the four multivariate factors
is given in @tbl-legend.

## Screening design

Factor screening will use a two-level full factorial in the four multivariate factors
(A–D) with three centre-point replicates, `{python} n_scr` runs in total. The full
factorial estimates all four main effects and all six two-factor interactions without
confounding. Three responses will be recorded for each run (eluate-pool aggregate,
eluate-pool HCP and step yield). The planned coded design is given in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The four multivariate factors will be carried into a face-centred central-composite
design with four centre-point replicates, `{python} n_rsm` runs in total, enabling
estimation of curvature in addition to main effects and interactions. The planned coded
design is given in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

The elution flow rate will be evaluated one factor at a time across its characterization
range for its effect on step yield, the eluate-pool aggregate and HCP, and the
chromatographic profile; it will not be carried into the multivariate design because
prior knowledge indicates no credible impact to a product-quality CQA.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

The study is acceptable when:

1. the SDM qualification confirms representativeness of commercial scale
   (**SOP-1001**);
2. the fitted response-surface models for the eluate-pool aggregate and the eluate-pool
   HCP are adequate — target R² ≥ 0.90, adjusted R² ≥ 0.80, no significant lack of fit
   (p > 0.05 against the centre-point pure error), and residual diagnostics without
   systematic structure (a response governed by a single dominant factor is reported by
   that dependence and is otherwise robust); and
3. a multivariate operating region exists over which the eluate-pool aggregate and HCP are
   controlled at the set-point and across each parameter's NOR.

Each parameter will then be classified per the A-Mab continuum [@amab2009]:

- a parameter whose variability significantly impacts a CQA is a **CPP**; where the
  impact is reliably controlled within the operating region (low risk of leaving it)
  the parameter is a **well-controlled CPP (WC-CPP)**;
- a parameter that does not significantly impact a CQA but affects process performance
  or consistency is a **KPP**; otherwise it is a **GPP**;
- consistent with the post-characterization FMEA convention, a parameter that affects a
  CQA with Severity ≥ 8, or that carries an initial (pre-mitigation) risk priority
  number > 72, is designated a CPP before mitigation by the control strategy.

The operating region, classifications and PARs established here will justify the
Stage 2 operating ranges and feed the drug-substance control strategy.

# Data management and integrity

All raw data, DoE designs, analytical results and statistical analyses will be recorded
and retained under the site data-integrity procedures (ALCOA+). Analyses will be
performed with version-controlled scripts and reviewed by a second analyst; designs,
models and the derived operating region will be archived with the report. Any deviation
from this plan will be documented and assessed for impact in PCR-007.

: Roles and responsibilities. {#tbl-roles}

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable of this plan is the Process Characterization Report (**PCR-007**),
reporting the executed designs, the significant effects, the operating region, the
parameter classification and the aggregate/impurity-CQA outcomes. PCR-007 rolls up into
the Process Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**) and provides the parameter risk
basis for the post-characterization process risk assessment. Execution follows SDM
qualification and precedes the Stage 2 PPQ campaign.

# Risks and assumptions

The plan assumes the SDM is representative of commercial scale (confirmed by
qualification) and that the platform analytical methods are validated and in control. The
principal risk is that the absolute aggregate and HCP clearance shift at commercial scale
or over the resin life-cycle, or that the incoming aggregate load is higher than
characterized; this is mitigated by defining the operating region on the qualified SDM,
challenging the step against a representative worst-case aggregate feed, confirming the
region at scale in Stage 2, and carrying the WC-CPP ranges forward with in-process
monitoring and resin life-cycle control.
